requirements.original: c) All formal parameters of the function or altstep invoked in a call test component operation shall be of a component data type.
requirements.canonical: Every formal parameter of the function or altstep invoked in a `call` operation SHALL be of a component data type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- c) All formal parameters of the function or altstep invoked in a call test component operation shall be of a component data type.

requirements.original: d) The return value of the function invoked from a call test component operation shall be of a component data type.
requirements.canonical: The return type of the function invoked in a `call` operation SHALL be a component data type.

ambiguity.issue: The restriction concerns the return type, but 'return value' is used.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- d) The return value of the function invoked from a call test component operation shall be of a component data type.

requirements.original: e) The optional SimpleExpression representing the timer value shall be of a float type.
requirements.canonical: The optional SimpleExpression giving the timeout duration of a `call` operation SHALL be of type `float`.

ambiguity.issue: The semantic description calls it 'timeout duration', the restriction 'timer value' although no timer is involved.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- e) The optional SimpleExpression representing the timer value shall be of a float type.

requirements.original: f) The optional catch `timeout clause may be present only if the timeout value has been defined.`
requirements.canonical: A `catch(timeout)` clause SHALL NOT be present in a `call` operation unless a timeout duration is given.

ambiguity.issue: 'timeout value' is used instead of 'timeout duration'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- f) The optional catch `timeout clause may be present only if the timeout value has been defined.`

requirements.original: g) The variable in the value clause shall be compatible with the return value of the invoked function.
requirements.canonical: The variable in the `value` clause of a `call` operation SHALL be compatible with the return type of the invoked function.

ambiguity.issue: Compatibility is a property of types; 'return value' is used where the return type is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- g) The variable in the value clause shall be compatible with the return value of the invoked function.

requirements.original: h) The variable in the verdict clause shall be of type verdicttype.
requirements.canonical: The variable in the `verdict` clause of a `call` operation SHALL be of type `verdicttype`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- h) The variable in the verdict clause shall be of type verdicttype.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports message-based and procedure-based _unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS supporting message-based unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.0 -- TTCN-3 supports message-based and procedure-based _unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports message-based and procedure-based _unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS supporting procedure-based unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.0 -- TTCN-3 supports message-based and procedure-based _unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.

requirements.original: Furthermore,_ TTCN-3 allows to examine the top element of incoming port queues and to control the access to ports by means of _controlling operations.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language CAN examine the top element of an incoming port queue.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.0 -- Furthermore,_ TTCN-3 allows to examine the top element of incoming port queues and to control the access to ports by means of _controlling operations.

requirements.original: Furthermore,_ TTCN-3 allows to examine the top element of incoming port queues and to control the access to ports by means of _controlling operations.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language CAN control the access to a port by means of controlling operations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.0 -- Furthermore,_ TTCN-3 allows to examine the top element of incoming port queues and to control the access to ports by means of _controlling operations.

requirements.original: Message-based communication is non-blocking on the send operation, as illustrated in figure 11, where processing in the SENDER continues immediately after the send operation occurs.
requirements.canonical: The `send` operation IS non-blocking: processing in the sender SHALL continue immediately after the `send` operation occurs.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.1 -- Message-based communication is non-blocking on the send operation, as illustrated in figure 11, where processing in the SENDER continues immediately after the send operation occurs.

requirements.original: The RECEIVER is blocked on the receive operation until it processes the received message.
requirements.canonical: The `receive` operation IS blocking: the receiver is blocked on the `receive` operation until it processes the received message.

readings: The receiver is blocked on the `receive` operation until a matching message has been received and processed.
The receiver is blocked on the `receive` operation until any message arrives in the port queue.
ambiguity.issue: 'until it processes the received message' does not state whether the message must match; chosen reading: blocked until a matching message is processed (consistent with the alt/snapshot semantics in clause 20).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.1 -- The RECEIVER is blocked on the receive operation until it processes the received message.

requirements.original: In addition to the receive operation, TTCN-3 provides a trigger operation that filters messages with certain matching criteria from a stream of received messages on a given incoming port.
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation IS filtering messages that fulfil given matching criteria from the stream of received messages on a given incoming port.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.1 -- In addition to the receive operation, TTCN-3 provides a trigger operation that filters messages with certain matching criteria from a stream of received messages on a given incoming port.

requirements.original: Messages at the top of the queue that do not fulfil the matching criteria are removed from the port without any further action.
requirements.canonical: When the `trigger` operation is executed, a message at the top of the port queue that does not fulfil the matching criteria IS removed from the port queue without any further action.
requirements.condition: the message at the top of the queue does not match the trigger's matching criteria

ambiguity.issue: messages are removed from the port queue, not from the port itself.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.1 -- Messages at the top of the queue that do not fulfil the matching criteria are removed from the port without any further action.
